chapter.v:
A man
who isolates himself seeks his own desire;He rages against all wise judgment. [[Lam. 3:44]] [Matt. 11:23 c]

A fool
has no delight in understanding,But in expressing his own heart. [Ps. 21:9; Lam. 3:43 f Ps. 89:39, 40; Is. 43:28]

When the
wicked comes, contempt comes also;And with dishonor comes reproach. [Ps. 74:11; Jer. 21:4, 5 h Ps. 89:46]

The words
of a man’s mouth are deep waters;The wellspring of wisdom is a flowing brook. [Ezek. 24:25] [Is. 63:10]

It is
not good to show partiality to the wicked,Or to overthrow the righteous in judgment. [Jer. 30:14 l 2 Kin. 25:9; Jer. 52:13; Lam. 2:2]

A fool’s
lips enter into contention,And his mouth calls for blows. [Ps. 80:12; 89:40; Is. 5:5; Jer. 7:14 n Is. 1:8; Jer. 52:13 o Is. 43:28]

A fool’s
mouth is his destruction,And his lips are the snare of his soul. [Ezek. 24:21] [Ps. 74:3-8]

The words
of a talebearer are like tasty trifles,And they go down into the inmost body. [Jer. 52:14 s [2 Kin. 21:13; Is. 34:11; Amos 7:7-9]]

He who
is slothful in his workIs a brother to him who is a great destroyer. [Deut. 28:36; 2 Kin. 24:15; 25:7; Lam. 1:3; 4:20 v 2 Chr. 15:3] [Ps. 74:9; Mic.]

The name
of the Lord is a strong tower;The righteous run to it and are safe. [Job 2:13; Is. 3:26 y Job 2:12; Ezek. 27:30 z Is. 15:3; Jon. 3:6-8 7 A]

The rich
man’s wealth is his strong city,And like a high wall in his own esteem. [Ps. 6:7; Lam. 3:48 b Job 16:13; Ps. 22:14 c Lam.]

Before destruction
the heart of a man is haughty,And before honor is humility.

He who
answers a matter before he hears it,It is folly and shame to him. [Lam. 1:12; Dan. 9:12]

The spirit
of a man will sustain him in sickness,But who can bear a broken spirit? [Jer. 2:8; 23:25- Ezek. 13:2 f Is. 58:1; Ezek. 23:36; Mic. 3:8 g Jer. 23:33-36; Ezek.]

The heart
of the prudent acquires knowledge,And the ear of the wise seeks knowledge. [1 Kin. 9:8; Job 27:23; Jer. 18:16; Ezek. 25:6; Nah. 3:19 i 2 Kin. 19:21; Ps. 44:14 j [Ps. 48:2; 50:2]; Ezek.]

A man’s
gift makes room for him,And brings him before great men. [Lam. 1:21; [Obad. 12-15] n Ps.] [Job 16:9, 10; Ps. 22:13; Lam. 3:46 l Ps. 56:2; 124:3; Jer. 51:34]

The first
one to plead his cause seems right,Until his neighbor comes and examines him. [Lev. 26:16] [Ps. 38:16]

Casting lots
causes contentions to cease,And keeps the mighty apart. [Jer. 14:17;]

A brother
offended is harder to win than a strong city,And contentions are like the bars of a castle. [Ps. 119:147 s]

A man’s
stomach shall be satisfied from the fruit of his mouth;From the produce of his lips he shall be filled. [Lev. 26:29; Deut. 28:53; Jer. 19:9; Lam. 4:10; Ezek. 5:10 5 Vg. a]

Death and
life are in the power of the tongue,And those who love it will eat its fruit. [2 Chr. 36:17; Jer. 6:11 w Jer.]

He who
finds a wife finds a good thing,And obtains favor from the Lord. [Ps. 31:13; Is. 24:17; Jer. 6:25] [Hos. 9:12 z Jer.]

The poor
man uses entreaties,But the rich answers roughly.

A man
who has friends must himself be friendly,But there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
